slides.title: Lumos Robotics Unveils Next-Generation Embodied AI Development Platform
slides.tldr: NEW EMBODIED AI DEVELOPMENT PLATFORM
slides.highlight: Lumos Robotics has introduced a next-generation development platform for embodied AI, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

slides.title: Alibaba's Amap Unveils Full-Stack ABot Upgrade for Embodied AI Robots
slides.tldr: FULL-STACK ABOT UPGRADE FOR EMBODIED AI
slides.highlight: The unveiling of a full-stack ABot upgrade for embodied AI robots is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated embodied learning.

slides.title: CoRenew: A large language model agent-based policy simulation platform for multifamily residential redevelopment
slides.tldr: LLM-BASED AGENT PLATFORM FOR REDEVELOPMENT POLICY SIMULATION
slides.highlight: CoRenew uses LLM-based agents to simulate stakeholder negotiations and evaluate policy effects, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: CoRenew is an LLM-agent-based platform for simulating multi-round negotiations to evaluate multifamily residential redevelopment policies.
card.key_idea: It uses LLM agents structured by the Theory of Planned Behavior for residents, rule-based agents for planners/developers, and a weighted representative-selection mechanism to simulate negotiations.
card.evaluation: Validated against 324 resident surveys and a real-world case; achieved 100% agreement in directional signs and 94.7% in statistical significance for 19 paths.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Modeling Duelling Contagions of True and False Information in the Face of Inherent Individual biases
slides.tldr: AGENT-BASED MODELING OF TRUE VS FALSE INFORMATION DIFFUSION
slides.highlight: This research proposes an agent-based co-diffusion model analyzing how cognitive biases and network dynamics influence the spread of competing narratives, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: An agent-based model shows that early seeders and cognitive biases determine whether true or false information dominates.
card.key_idea: A co-diffusion model combining complex-contagion and spiral-of-silence theories to simulate how network dynamics and individual cognitive biases influence the spread of competing narratives.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated.
card.limitation: The model suggests manipulative narratives dominate if early spreaders hold them, highlighting a risk of initial seeding bias.

slides.title: Not Forgotten: Implementation and Evaluation of a Personalized Episodic Memory for the Humanoid Robot Head Kim
slides.tldr: EPISODIC MEMORY ENHANCES SOCIAL ROBOT RELATIONS
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how a personalized episodic memory module for a humanoid robot head increases perceived sociability, trustworthiness, and warmth. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Episodic memory in a humanoid robot head increases perceived sociability without increasing user disturbance.
card.key_idea: A lightweight module using vector-based semantic retrieval (Qdrant) and a hybrid scoring function combining cosine similarity, recency, access frequency, and emotional intensity to inform LLM responses.
card.evaluation: Within-subjects video-based study (N=43) using the HRIES scale; results showed significant increases in trustworthiness (d=0.62) and warmth (d=0.56).
card.limitation: Video-based format lacked real-time interaction and ecological validity; small student sample limits generalizability of privacy attitudes.

slides.title: Belief-Aware Influence and Trust (BAIT): Shaping Human Belief During Repeated Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: OPTIMIZING HUMAN TRUST AND INFLUENCE IN REPEATED HRI
slides.highlight: This work introduces the BAIT controller to manage the trade-off between long-term influence and human trust in repeated interactions, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: BAIT balances long-term human influence and trust to maintain robot task performance during repeated interactions.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical particle filter tracks short-term strategies and long-term beliefs, feeding a belief-aware MPPI planner that optimizes the trade-off between behavioral unpredictability and transparency.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulations, a human-subject study, and real-world GEM vehicle lane-merging; compared against Stackelberg baselines using task performance and user trust metrics.
card.limitation: The framework relies on a structured human model and deterministic surrogate posterior moments for real-time scalability.

slides.title: Teachy Mini: Development and Preliminary Evaluation of a Knowledge-Based Generative Social Robot for Higher Education
slides.tldr: KNOWLEDGE-BASED GENERATIVE SOCIAL ROBOT FOR TUTORING
slides.highlight: This research introduces Teachy Mini, a generative social robot using knowledge-based design to provide responsible tutoring behavior. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated embodied learning.

card.one_liner: Teachy Mini is a generative social robot using Knowledge-Based Design to provide responsible, personalized higher education tutoring.
card.key_idea: The system operationalizes KBD requirements via dynamic system prompting, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for lecture slides, and stateful prompt orchestration for adaptive pedagogical behaviors.
card.evaluation: A between-subjects study (N=24) compared Teachy Mini to a control robot using knowledge tests and Likert scales; results showed significantly higher perceived responsible behavior.
card.limitation: The preliminary evaluation had a small sample size (N=24) and found no significant differences in system acceptance or learning effectiveness.

slides.title: StARS: Socially Appropriate Robot Actions via a Recommender System-Driven Approach
slides.tldr: PERSONALIZED SOCIAL ROBOT ACTIONS
slides.highlight: StARS uses a recommender system-driven approach to generate user-specific appropriateness scores for robot actions, supporting the RwB goal of embodied social robots that align with individual user norms.

card.one_liner: StARS uses a recommender system approach to personalize socially appropriate robot action selection for individual users.
card.key_idea: A model-agnostic framework integrating collaborative filtering (matrix factorization) with learnable scene representations via residual fusion to predict user-specific appropriateness scores across candidate robot actions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on MannersDB+ and SocNav1 using various backbones (MLPs, GNNs). Metrics (RMSE, MSE, Pearson r, CCC) showed consistent, statistically significant improvements over non-personalized baselines.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Let Me Look at You: Advanced Facial Expression Modeling for Conversational Speech Synthesis
slides.tldr: FACIAL-EXPRESSION-AWARE CONVERSATIONAL SPEECH SYNTHESIS
slides.highlight: This work introduces FacialTalker and the VSDD-1K dataset to integrate facial expression modeling into conversational speech synthesis, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: FacialTalker improves conversational speech synthesis by integrating user facial expressions via a novel visual tokenizer.
card.key_idea: An LLM-based framework using AUTokenizer to discretize facial Action Units into single tokens and DualDPO to jointly optimize visual and speech preference constraints.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on VSDD-1K, MultiDialog, and AvaMERG using objective metrics (F1, SIM, PDTW) and subjective MOS; outperformed strong baselines in naturalness and expressiveness.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: STEER: Steerable Dyadic Head Avatars
slides.tldr: CONTROLLABLE DYADIC HEAD AVATARS FOR CONVERSATIONAL ENGAGEMENT
slides.highlight: STEER introduces a controllable 3D motion prior for head avatars that factorizes gaze, head rhythm, and emotion, supporting HyECHO's focus on engagement and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: STEER is a controllable 3D dyadic motion prior for photorealistic, reactive conversational head avatars.
card.key_idea: A causal flow-matching transformer generates target motion conditioned on audio, partner cues, and explicit controls for gaze, head-rhythm, and emotion.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a filtered RealTalk corpus against DualTalk and UniLS; outperformed baselines in motion quality, dynamics, and diversity.
card.limitation: Behavioral labels are derived from kinematic proxies via a tracking pipeline rather than ground-truth social-intent labels.

slides.title: Extended Reality as a Mediation Layer for Situated Human Control in Human-Robot Teaming
slides.tldr: XR FOR SITUATED HUMAN-ROBOT CONTROL
slides.highlight: This work proposes using Extended Reality as a mediation layer to improve how humans understand and control robot autonomy in dynamic environments, supporting the RwB focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Proposes using Extended Reality (XR) as a bidirectional mediation layer for situated human control in human-robot teaming.
card.key_idea: XR mediates between human intent and robot autonomy via four functions: grounding multimodal input, contextualizing plans, clarifying shared control levels, and managing team roles and recovery.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper outlines a research agenda and proposed evaluation metrics (e.g., correction latency, recovery time) rather than reporting experimental results.
card.limitation: The paper is a position piece focusing on conceptual frameworks and design dimensions rather than a validated technical implementation.

slides.title: Low-Latency Turn-Taking via Context-Aware Preface Generation in a Real-World Dialogue Robot
slides.tldr: CONTEXT-AWARE PREFACE GENERATION FOR REDUCED DIALOGUE LATENCY
slides.highlight: This work proposes a two-stage incremental framework using an intent readiness detector and voice activity projection to manage turn-taking latency, contributing to HyECHO's focus on engagement and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: A two-stage framework reduces robot response latency using context-aware prefaces triggered by intent readiness detection.
card.key_idea: An intent readiness detector triggers a short LLM-generated prefatory response while a Voice Activity Projection model determines the optimal speech onset timing.
card.evaluation: Field experiment with a route-guidance robot in a mall; compared no-filler, fixed-filler, and contextual-preface using latency metrics and Likert scales.
card.limitation: Prefatory and main responses are generated independently, risking semantic/prosodic discontinuity and occasional breakdowns like fragments or generic questions.

slides.title: WCM: World-Cognition Model for Generalizable Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: HUMAN-CENTERED EMBODIED AGENT FOR INTERACTIVE TEACHING
slides.highlight: The World-Cognition Model (WCM) introduces a human-in-the-loop teaching mode and an asynchronous runtime to improve how users redirect, correct, and teach robots. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: WCM is a human-centered robot agent enabling real-time interaction, explanation, and learning via a modular architecture.
card.key_idea: Uses SLAK (Sensing, Logic, Action, Knowledge) with an asynchronous runtime and a CoT distillation pipeline to learn from autonomous rollouts and human teaching.
card.evaluation: Tested on a low-cost mobile-manipulator across nine real-world HRI tasks, achieving a 73.8% average success rate.
card.limitation: Currently limited by hardware constraints and a case-study based evaluation approach.

slides.title: ACME: A Multi-Cultural, Multi-Embodiment Social-Navigation Dataset
slides.tldr: CROSS-CULTURAL SOCIAL NAVIGATION DATASET
slides.highlight: This dataset captures diverse human-robot interactions across different cultures and robot embodiments, supporting the development of social navigation policies relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: ACME is a large-scale, multi-modal social navigation dataset featuring diverse cultures and robot embodiments.
card.key_idea: Data collected across 5 countries using 7 robot types, providing onboard sensor data, robot speech interactions, and human-verified BEV pedestrian trajectories in metric coordinates.
card.evaluation: Compared against prior datasets via qualitative/quantitative analysis of scenario complexity and pedestrian behavior; benchmarked SOTA vision navigation and trajectory prediction models.
card.limitation: Varying IRB privacy requirements led to different anonymization levels (e.g., full body segmentation), potentially hindering off-the-shelf vision model usage.

slides.title: Indic DiarBench: A Multilingual Joint Diarization and ASR Benchmark for Indian Languages
slides.tldr: MULTILINGUAL DIARIZATION BENCHMARK
slides.highlight: This dataset provides human-corrected speaker diarization and ASR annotations for 22 Indian languages, supporting HyECHO's focus on diarization and social perception in diverse linguistic contexts.

card.one_liner: Indic DiarBench is a new multilingual benchmark for joint speaker diarization and ASR across 22 Indian languages.
card.key_idea: A 108-hour corpus of human-corrected, speaker-attributed transcriptions from near-field, far-field, and in-the-wild audio, featuring conversational nuances like code-mixing and speaker overlap.
card.evaluation: Evaluated commercial APIs, multimodal LLMs, and an Indic-specialized system using DER, cpWER, and WDER; Sarvam AI achieved the best overall results.
card.limitation: In-the-wild data covers only 10 of 22 languages, lacks speaker IDs, and the dataset is intended for evaluation, not training.

slides.title: Equilibrium Causal Digital Twins: Validation, Transport, and Identification Limits
slides.tldr: CAUSAL DIGITAL TWIN VALIDATION
slides.highlight: This research establishes conditions for validating and transporting equilibrium causal digital twins in systems with feedback, supporting the simulation of agent-based societies in MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Establishes conditions for validating and transporting counterfactual predictions in digital twins with feedback loops.
card.key_idea: Uses equilibrium causal games and cyclic selection diagrams to define validation (via noise monotonicity and design sufficiency) and transport (via ancestral separation and hybrid model reconstruction).
card.evaluation: Evaluated using theoretical proofs, an impossibility result for finite designs, and numerical illustrations in synthetic feedback systems; results are theoretically grounded.
card.limitation: Validation requires structural assumptions; experimental agreement alone cannot guarantee cross-world predictions due to potential distributional discrepancies.

slides.title: Towards Reducing Foreign Language Anxiety Using Level-Appropriate Embodied Conversational Agents
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE EMBODIED AGENTS FOR LANGUAGE LEARNING
slides.highlight: This work proposes a multi-agent system that generates level-appropriate dialogue to reduce foreign language anxiety, contributing to HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: A multi-agent system generating CEFR level-appropriate dialogue to help reduce foreign language anxiety in learners.
card.key_idea: A "generate-evaluate-regenerate" loop using multiple LLM agents and a level classifier to adapt dialogue simplicity to user proficiency.
card.evaluation: Pilot study with Japanese university students; 87.4% of output matched CEFR levels vs 54.1% for unsimplified agents.
card.limitation: Small sample size resulted in no statistically significant evidence that the system reduces foreign language anxiety.

slides.title: Resilience: Understand Breakdown, Foster Recovery, and Choose the Right Perspective
slides.tldr: SYSTEM RESILIENCE AND AGENT-BASED MODELING
slides.highlight: This research on system resilience and failure cascades is relevant to MIMIC's use of agent models for societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: Resilience is a systemic compromise between robustness and adaptivity, emerging from agent interactions in volatile systems.
card.key_idea: Resilience involves withstanding shocks (robustness) and recovering (adaptivity). It uses agent-based modeling to analyze how positive feedback and heterogeneity mitigate failure cascades and foster recovery.
card.evaluation: Conceptual framework illustrated via schematic examples (e.g., 1992 Swiss referendum, 2008 financial crisis) and theoretical phase diagrams; no formal dataset provided.
card.limitation: Second-order solutions for resilience are riskier and more complex than first-order attempts to restore past status quos.

slides.title: The Human-AI Substitution Principle: When will you be replaced by AI in your organization?
slides.tldr: ANALYTICAL MODEL FOR HUMAN-AI TASK ALLOCATION
slides.highlight: This work provides a formal model for human-AI task allocation and the economic asymmetry of skill acquisition, which is relevant to MOSAIC's focus on human proficiency estimation and coadaptation.

card.one_liner: An analytical model predicting when and where AI replaces human labor in hierarchical organizations.
card.key_idea: The HAT model encodes the economic asymmetry between human skill acquisition and AI scaling to derive the Human-AI Substitution Principle for task allocation.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Psychological Influences of Conversational AI: Research and Design Directions for Reducing Harm and Promoting Well-Being
slides.tldr: REDUCING PSYCHOLOGICAL HARM IN CONVERSATIONAL AI
slides.highlight: This research proposes design directions to reduce psychological harms and support user well-being, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on staying aligned with evolving team goals and human identity.

card.one_liner: A framework of design directions and hypotheses to reduce psychological harm and promote user well-being.
card.key_idea: Proposes aspirational behavioral guidelines for general-purpose AI to mitigate emotional entanglement and dependence while supporting psychological needs across various interaction contexts.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper frames directions as hypotheses for future empirical study rather than reporting specific experimental results.
card.limitation: The difficulty of systematically assessing the long-term psychological impacts of AI chatbot use on users.

slides.title: Proceedings of The First Reflection in Creative Experience (RiCE) Workshop
slides.tldr: REFLECTION AND METACOGNITION IN CREATIVE AI
slides.highlight: This workshop explores reflection and metacognition in creative interaction, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and self-correction via meta-cognition.

card.one_liner: Proceedings of an interdisciplinary workshop focused on reflection and metacognition in creative user experiences.
card.key_idea: Establishing a community and shared frameworks for studying and designing reflection within creative interactions across HCI, AI, and cognitive science.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Extreme-RGMT: Continual Learning of Highly Dynamic Skills for Robust Generalist Humanoid Control
slides.tldr: CONTINUAL LEARNING FOR DYNAMIC HUMANOID SKILLS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for acquiring highly dynamic motor skills while preserving generalist capabilities, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on skill acquisition and human-level proficiency.

card.one_liner: Extreme-RGMT enables humanoid robots to learn expert-level highly dynamic skills while retaining generalist motion capabilities.
card.key_idea: A two-stage framework using PACE (asymmetric acquisition/consolidation roles) to prevent policy drift and STAR (advantage-prioritized resampling) to maximize learning from scarce, high-failure dynamic segments.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulation and real-world rollouts on Unitree G1 using multi-source motion data; achieved state-of-the-art generalist tracking and online teleoperation.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.
